title: What can the measure of this acute angle be?
description: Four times the measure must stay under ninety degrees and five times must go past ninety. Together these keep the measure between eighteen and twenty two and a half degrees, which gives nineteen, twenty, twenty one and twenty two in whole degrees.
teaching_notes: One idea: write each clue as a limit on the measure, then keep only what satisfies all of them. Watch for students who check only one clue, or who count ninety as acute or obtuse.

source: Figure it Out box 2, Q7, Puzzle
video_script.why: The child turns each clue into a limit, finds that the biggest acute multiple and the obtuse multiple give the two ends of a range, and lists the whole degrees inside it.
video_script.substitution: 4 times the measure is less than 90, so the measure is less than 22.5; 5 times the measure is more than 90, so it is more than 18; whole degrees are 19, 20, 21, 22.
video_script.anchor: a strip of degrees from 0 to 180 with 90 marked
video_script.payoff_line: Two conditions together give one range

final_answer.spoken: in whole degrees, my measure is nineteen, twenty, twenty one or twenty two

never_show: a claim that the measure must be exactly one number
maths_rules: acute: less than 90°; obtuse: more than 90° and less than 180°
2m < 3m < 4m, so 4m < 90° is the only acute condition needed
check with m = 20: 40, 60, 80 acute and 100 obtuse
video_script.design: One strip of degrees. The acute limit is shaded teal from the left, the obtuse limit is shaded amber from the right, and the overlap is boxed.
open_questions: The question does not say whole degrees; the book answer lists 19, 20, 21 and 22, so the video gives the range first and then the whole-degree values.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a speech bubble from an angle: I am acute; double me, triple me, four times me: acute; five times me: obtuse

marks.book: the title card From your book appears
marks.angle: an angle speaks from a bubble: I am an acute angle
marks.acute: the bubble adds: double, triple and four times my measure are acute again
marks.obtuse: the bubble adds: five times my measure is obtuse, and a question mark glows

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a puzzle from your book.
<bookmark mark='angle'/>An acute angle speaks.
<bookmark mark='acute'/>Double my measure, triple it, or take four times it, and you still get an acute angle.
<bookmark mark='obtuse'/>But five times my measure is obtuse. What can my measure be?

beats.on_screen: the bubble holds still on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a strip from 0° to 180°; the part before 90° is labelled acute and the part from 90° to 180° is labelled obtuse; a measure is marked and moves along the strip when it is multiplied

marks.strip: a strip from 0° to 180° is drawn with 90° marked in the middle
marks.acute: the part before 90° is labelled acute
marks.obtuse: the part between 90° and 180° is labelled obtuse
marks.grow: a mark is multiplied and slides to the right along the strip

narration: <bookmark mark='strip'/>Look at a strip of degrees from zero to one hundred eighty.
<bookmark mark='acute'/>Before ninety, an angle is acute.
<bookmark mark='obtuse'/>Between ninety and one hundred eighty, it is obtuse.
<bookmark mark='grow'/>When we multiply a measure, its mark slides to the right.

beats.on_screen: Given: m is acute; 2m, 3m, 4m are acute; 5m is obtuse
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, my measure and its double, triple and four times are acute, and five times is obtuse.

beats.on_screen: To find: the possible measures m

marks.find: the words possible measures are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the possible measures.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: 2m < 3m < 4m, so if 4m is acute, then 2m and 3m are acute too; only 4m < 90° is needed

marks.order: the marks for 2m, 3m and 4m are placed on the strip in order, 4m furthest right
marks.only: 4m is boxed, and the marks to its left are shaded acute

narration: <bookmark mark='order'/>Step one, four times my measure is the biggest of the three.
<bookmark mark='only'/>If that is acute, the double and the triple are acute as well.
We only need four times my measure to be less than ninety.

marks.find: 4 × 22.5° = 90° is written, with 90° on the strip
marks.less: m < 22.5° is written, and the part of the strip to the left is shaded teal

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>Step two, four times twenty two and a half is ninety.
<bookmark mark='less'/>Four times my measure must be less than ninety. My measure must be less than twenty two and a half.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 5m is obtuse, so 5m > 90°; 5 × 18° = 90°, so m > 18°

marks.five: 5m is placed past 90° on the strip
marks.more: m > 18° is written, and the part of the strip to the right of 18° is shaded amber

narration: <bookmark mark='five'/>Step three, five times my measure is obtuse, so it is more than ninety.
<bookmark mark='line'/>Five times eighteen is ninety.
<bookmark mark='more'/>My measure must be more than eighteen.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: both conditions: m is more than 18° and less than 22.5°; 5m is also under 180°

marks.both: the teal part and the amber part overlap between 18° and 22.5°
marks.range: the overlap is boxed: more than 18° and less than 22.5°

narration: <bookmark mark='both'/>Step four, put the two conditions together.
<bookmark mark='range'/>My measure is more than eighteen and less than twenty two and a half.
Five times it stays under one hundred eighty, so that is fine.

beats.on_screen: Step 5: check with 20°: 40°, 60°, 80° are acute; 100° is obtuse. At 18° the 5m is 90°, at 23° the 4m is 92°

marks.five: 100° lands after 90°, and is labelled obtuse
marks.edges: 18° gives 90° for five times, and 23° gives 92° for four times, and both are crossed out

narration: <bookmark mark='test'/>Step five, put the answer back in the question.
Try twenty degrees. Double is forty, triple is sixty, and four times is eighty. All are acute.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Five times is one hundred, which is obtuse.
<bookmark mark='edges'/>Eighteen fails, because five times it is only ninety. Twenty three fails, because four times it is ninety two.

beats.on_screen: Answer: m is more than 18° and less than 22.5°; in whole degrees: 19°, 20°, 21° and 22°

marks.pay: the words two conditions glow together
marks.range: the range between 18° and 22.5° is boxed on the strip
marks.whole: the whole-degree values in the range are marked and labelled

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>Two conditions together give one range.
<bookmark mark='range'/>My measure can be any value more than eighteen and less than twenty two and a half degrees.
<bookmark mark='whole'/>In whole degrees, it is nineteen, twenty, twenty one or twenty two.
